items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I think he probably gave a couple of notes you know, to work off of, to McCoy and off they went.

ctx.x: I wondered on occasion if the musicians like yourself and the fellas you mentioned sat around and talked about how they were going to play. Was there discussions that said like we might say, all right, we’re not going to play in this particular time signature, we’re just going to see what happens? Or I guess what I’m trying to say was any of this music pre-planned before you got on the bandstand or did it happen as it was being created?

I would imagine some of it did happen as it was being created, that whoever was the band leader said, you know, this is, you know, these couple of notes or whatever, maybe. Let’s just work off of that and, you know, see what we get. You know John Coltrane, I mean we all got a chance to watch that develop you know, from the beginning when he put that quartet together, finally, who were going to be in it for that run ‘til his death. And they rehearsed you know. And when it got to the point when he decided he wanted…
